name: Turmeric and curcumin
short: Case series link turmeric supplements to liver injury, sometimes severe. Curcumin may alter levels of some drugs, including anticoagulants, mostly in non-clinical studies.
text: Case series describe liver injury after turmeric supplements: the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network found 10 cases, typically hepatocellular, appearing 1 to 4 months after starting, with five hospitalised and one death from acute liver failure, and an Italian series of 7 cases involved high-bioavailability, high-dose curcumin products. A review of interactions reports that curcumin can change blood levels of drugs including cardiovascular drugs, antidepressants, anticoagulants, antibiotics and chemotherapy agents, mainly by inhibiting CYP enzymes and P-glycoprotein; this evidence comes mostly from in vitro and in vivo studies, with only one clinical trial.
